chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Overcharging the band at restaurants and hotels
summary: Restaurants removed menus and a Birmingham hotel charged five dollars a night to a band, which led to the next story.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

So the girl would take off the menu.
Chick say, "Where you taking that menu?" That'll
give them a chance to raise the price, you know.
The meals were two dollars and something,
they could charge us three dollars. They give us
(inaudible) --

"What you got to eat
today? Where's the menu?
They say, "Oh, these are old menus."
They probably took the menu off the
table when we come in. That was kind of funny.
We used to laugh at funny things like that.
"Here come the band," you know.
Same way at the hotel. Like we stayed
in Birmingham. We stayed in the hotel -- Jewish
fella had the hotel there, all right?
When the band come in, he would charge
us like --
If you were paying twelve dollars a
week -- you stay there, right? You're living in a hotel

and you're only paying like twelve dollars a week or ten dollars a week.
Whatever you were paying, they would charge us that for a day. Five dollars a day.
And if you go in there and rent a room --
If you live there, you go in there and rent a room, he'll charge you a dollar and a half.
"Want to get a room for tonight? Yeah, give me two dollars."
When the band came in, he'd charge us like five dollars a day.
The man (inaudible) say, "How much he charged yall?"
But what we did the next time we came --
What do you think of that?
To us, that was always funny. That was a funny joke, because we always used to laugh about it.
